 Porsche Owners Told to Park Their Cars as Recall Grows Over Fracturing Wheel Locks
 By: 
 Saajan Jogia 
 Published: 
 October 23, 2026 - 3:02 pm 
 Saajan Jogia 
 October 23, 2026 
 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source 
 Porsche has recalled 548 vehicles across eight models after two additional incidents involving fractured center lock components were recorded, an issue that could cause a wheel to detach. The recall expands on NHTSA Recall No. 24V-809, filed in October 2024, which covered 2,251 vehicles.
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report 26V682 , the affected Porsche models include:
 2024 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS (73 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 Turbo S (94 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 Turbo (13 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 Turbo S/T (39 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 GT3 RS (41 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 GT3 (50 units)
 2024 Porsche 911 Carrera GTS (168 units)
 2024 Porsche 718 Spyder RS (70 units)
 Certain vehicles may have center wheel-lock parts that do not meet the required manufacturing specifications, making them susceptible to fracture. 
 If one of these components fails, the wheel could detach from the vehicle or the driver could experience diminished steering control. Either outcome could compromise vehicle stability and increase the risk of a crash, according to the report.
 File photo for illustration purposes. 
 The report identified the cause of the problem: 
 “Analyses of the affected material batch confirmed lead and bismuth contents outside the specification.”
 In May and August 2026, Porsche became aware of two additional incidents involving fractured center lock components. No injuries were reported.
 Further investigations with the supplier revealed gaps in the original traceability assessment due to previously unidentified material movements. Updated analyses suggested more components could be linked to the defective batch, prompting Porsche to expand the recall to additional vehicles.
 Owners are being advised not to drive the affected vehicles. A noticeable vibration may occur if a center lock component fractures, according to the report.
 Explaining the remedy program, the report stated:
 “Porsche will check the center lock wheel fastening system and replace any out-of-specification parts, if necessary.”
 “Owners will be contacted via phone, email, and MyPorsche App Push Notification in the coming 1-2 weeks to advise them of the Stop Drive order on the affected vehicles.”
 “Customer letters will be mailed to customers within the first 60 days after the filing of this report,” the report added.
 Porsche scheduled dealer notifications for October 20, 2026, while owner notifications are planned for December 15, 2026.
 The report states that reimbursement for pre-recall repairs is not applicable because all affected vehicles remain covered by Porsche’s New Car Limited Warranty.
